subject.title: Bug: Billing error (402) causes infinite retry death spiral for inline-apiKey providers (no backoff)

question: Should OpenClaw accept provider-scoped persisted cooldown state for inline `models.providers.<id>.apiKey` credentials, including fail-closed behavior during billing/auth cooldowns, as the fix for this issue?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but the durable inline-key cooldown namespace and fail-closed upgrade behavior are compatibility-sensitive auth-provider policy choices rather than a purely mechanical code change.

options.title: Accept provider-scoped cooldown after repair
options.body: Have the linked PR or a replacement rebase cleanly, preserve healthy auth-profile fallback, and explicitly own the persisted `inline-api-key:<provider>` cooldown contract.

options.title: Prefer synthetic auth profiles
options.body: Request a narrower design that maps inline keys into profile-like identities instead of adding a separate provider-scoped usage namespace.

options.title: Keep profile-only cooldowns
options.body: Decline the runtime behavior change and document migration to auth profiles as the supported recovery path, leaving inline keys outside billing cooldowns.

recommendation.title: Accept provider-scoped cooldown after repair
recommendation.body: Have the linked PR or a replacement rebase cleanly, preserve healthy auth-profile fallback, and explicitly own the persisted `inline-api-key:<provider>` cooldown contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is most tied to SecretRef/provider-auth compatibility, where this history shows recent relevant ownership.
